In Pandemic, several virulent diseases have broken out simultaneously all over the world! The players are disease-fighting specialists whose mission is to treat disease hotspots while researching cures for each of four plagues before they get out of hand. The game board depicts several major population centers on Earth. On each turn, a player can use up to four actions to travel between cities, treat infected populaces, discover a cure, or build a research station. A deck of cards provides the players with these abilities, but sprinkled throughout this deck are Epidemic! cards that accelerate and intensify the diseases' activity. A second, separate deck of cards controls the "normal" spread of the infections. Taking a unique role within the team, players must plan their strategy to mesh with their specialists' strengths in order to conquer the diseases. For example, the Operations Expert can build research stations which are needed to find cures for the diseases and which allow for greater mobility between cities; the Scientist needs only four cards of a particular disease to cure it instead of the normal five—but the diseases are spreading quickly and time is running out. If one or more diseases spreads beyond recovery or if too much time elapses, the players all lose. If they cure the four diseases, they all win! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Player Actions 2 Draw Cards 2.1 Epidemic Card 3 Infection 3.1 Outbreak 4 Events 5 Roles 6 Game End 7 Errata and Gotchas Player Actions Perform up to 4 actions per turn from the selections listed below. Move Drive/Ferry: Move to a city connected to the one you are in. Direct Flight: Discard a City card to move to the city named on the card. Charter Flight: Discard a City card with the name of the city you are in to move to any city. Shuttle Flight: Move from a city with a Research Station to any other city with a Research Station . Build a Research Station Discard a City card with the name of the city you are in to build a Research Station there. (Max of 6) Treat Disease Remove 1 disease cube from the city you are in. (If this disease has been cured, remove all cubes of that color.) Note: If the last cube of a cured disease is removed from the board, this disease is eradicated . Eradicated diseases are ignored when infection cards are drawn. Share Knowledge Either give the City card that matches the city you are in to another player or take the City card that matches the city you are in from another player. The other player must also be in the city with you. Both players must agree to do this. If the player who gets the card now has more than 7 cards, that player must immediately discard a card or play an Event card. Discover a Cure Discard 5 City cards of the same color from your hand to cure the disease of that color. A "cure token" will be placed on that disease's indicator on the board. You must be at a city with a Research Station, discard 5 City cards of the same colour from your hand to cure the disease of that color. If no cubes of that color are on the board, the disease is eradicated . The "cure token" is flipped to its "NO" side. Cured diseases still need to be treated. But during the "Treat Disease" action, you can remove all cubes of that disease from a city instead of just 1. Draw Cards After performed actions, draw two cards from the City pile into your hand. If your hand contains more than seven cards, discard cards or play Events until you have only seven. If the City pile runs out, the game ends and the players lose. Epidemic Card If you draw an EPIDEMIC! card, the following happens immediately: Infection Rate indicator is increased by 1. If this reaches the end, the game is over and the players lose. [Rating: 1/10] I hate the theme of this game.  It has some really interesting mechanisms, but I couldn't care less about the theme.

[Rating: 1/10] Very abstract, Theme is strange and not so catchy as Arkham Horror or Battlestar Galactica. Theme in Pandemic is dry. But its good way to test cooperative game mechanics to want buy next and better cooperative games as Arkham Horror:-)  Update. After some losses i Won and think yes, it would be interesting. But after three wins Ive got some strange feelengs. Are there something more to discover in this game or thats all folks?:-) from 7 to 6  update: From 6 to 3, after few games I found it very boring and not replayable.  update: absolutelly 1 point:-D

[Rating: 1/10] Stressful, challenging fun. Tough game to to win especially with +3 players. A good adult + kids game as everyone can play at full tilt and is short and structured enough to retain the young 'uns attention.

[Rating: 1/10] Luck-driven co-op game where experienced players will instruct you what the "correct" move is on your turn. Exceedingly boring and dry with predictable outcomes. Like a worse version of shadows over camelot.

[Rating: 1/10] it would've been good if it weren't for the stupid mechanic of reshuffling the cards and putting them back on top of the deck everytime an epidemic card is drawn. defenders of the realm is 100% better of a game, screw pandemic.

[Rating: 1/10] Boring! Pushing wood cubes around and eliminating them. Strategy is not hard at all, and often its irrelevant due to the card draw luck. Just horrible.

[Rating: 1/10] There are probably worse games than this, I will just have to find one.  + Production - Theme - Gameplay - Fully-Coop-Broken-Solitare-Game  It is actually a 3/10 game. Not a 1/10... but then again some games are just heavily overrated due to marketing and hype; so some underrating won't hurt.

[Rating: 1/10] I do not understand why people enjoy this game.  It is not fun nor interesting.  Cooperative games either turn into one of two things: 1) the person with the best ideas strategy tells everyone else what to do and its basically like playing alone, or 2) this person just watches people make poor decisions.  Either way it is not fun.  This is one of the few games if you asked me if I wanted to play I would say no.

[Rating: 1/10] If you are wondering why I rated this a "1", the answer is simple: it defies the description of a game (taken from BGG rating guidelines).
